texts: mixed: the rule fires and the storing, the clay vessels and the cauldron are all captured, but 'the Keepers' with a capital K is read as a bare proper name, so the storers carry no link to the keeper kind your other rules quantify over. Write 'When mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the keepers store the mire-essence in clay vessels.' - the lower-case plural records them as keepers and changes nothing else.

mixed: as with the 'when' version, the rule fires and everything is covered, but capitalised 'the Keepers' becomes a bare proper name with no link to the keeper kind the rest of your rules range over. Write 'Whenever mire-essence forms in the cauldron, the keepers keep the mire-essence in clay vessels.'

bad: the drawing is minted once per Keeper instead of once per tending, so a keeper who tends several lanterns is recorded as making a single draw that is somehow going on during all of them. Mixing the 'each Keeper' universal with a 'when that Keeper ...' clause is what pushed it there; write 'Whenever a Keeper tends a lantern, that Keeper draws the stored mire-essence.' - the plain whenever shape gives one drawing per tending and keeps the meaning intact.

mixed: the rule fires over any stored mire-essence, but 'will' was dropped, so it reads as a standing habit rather than the future claim you wrote. If the standing reading is what you mean, write 'Stored mire-essence feeds lantern lighting.' and the parse is then exactly right; if you mean a genuine prediction about the future, the future marker has to be restored on our side.
